OCA.label: Orthodox Church in America — Lives of the Saints
OCA.path: https://www.oca.org/saints/lives/{YYYY}/{MM}/{DD} — not in repo; web-addressable per day
OCA.notes: GOVERNING CALENDAR FOR THE EOR TAG, set by Josh 2026-09-05, on the same principle as the Church of the East: a communion/jurisdictional calendar decides the date. Fetchable and date-addressable, one civil day per URL. THROUGHPUT LIMIT, measured not assumed: the 356 unconfirmed EOR rows sit on 326 distinct days, so a full pass is 326 separate page fetches, and this environment can only reach a URL already linked from a page it has already fetched -- i.e. walking the Backward/Forward chain a day at a time. That is not a viable bulk pass. OCA is therefore the ADJUDICATING authority; a machine-readable baseline is needed to carry the bulk. CORRECTION 2026-09-05: an earlier version of this note asserted that Synaxarium-Constantinople.txt was "the obvious EOR equivalent" of the Coptic baseline. That was said before the file had been seen. It has now been read: it is Delehaye's 1902 Bollandist edition of a tenth-century Byzantine synaxarion, 82% Greek, and it is NOT a calendar. It is not registered as a witness on this project. No modern Eastern Orthodox machine-readable calendar is yet identified.

COPTIC_READER.label: Coptic Reader — Coptic Orthodox Metropolis of the Southern United States
COPTIC_READER.notes: GOVERNING CALENDAR FOR THE OOR TAG, set by Josh 2026-09-05. The Coptic Church is this project's first Oriental Orthodox tradition; Coptic Reader's Synaxarion Calendar, used with the Antiphonary/Difnar, is the fullest current U.S. diocesan source. A file named coptic-synaxarium.json.txt is said to exist and to be usable as the machine-readable baseline. CORRECTION 2026-09-05: an earlier version of this note stated that file contains "366 days, 702 entries" and omits the New Martyrs of Libya and St Maurice. THOSE FIGURES AND THAT GAP LIST WERE NEVER VERIFIED HERE. They came from a ChatGPT message Josh pasted into the conversation, and were repeated as though they were established fact. Nobody on this project has opened the file; Josh does not know where it came from. Nothing may be built on those numbers until the file is in hand and inspected.

ETH.label: Ethiopian Synaxarium
ETH.notes: Great Church / Oriental Orthodox source witness. SCOPED 2026-09-05: Ethiopian only, and Ethiopia is NOT this project's first Oriental Orthodox tradition -- the Coptic Church is (Josh, 2026-09-05). This witness does not speak for the OOR tag generally and must not be used to date Coptic, Armenian or Syriac commemorations.

ACOE_WE_2026.label: Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of Western Europe — Ecclesiastical Calendar 2026
ACOE_WE_2026.notes: MISLABELLED UNTIL 2026-09-05. Registered as COFE_2026, "English Calendar 2026", an "anglican_calendar_reference" -- on the strength of the filename alone, its own note conceding "exact source label to be refined if used." The file is not an English Anglican calendar. Its title page reads "Holy Apostolic Catholic Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of Western Europe -- Ecclesiastical Calendar 2026", with the Syriac heading above it and Mar Awa III and Mar Awraham Youkhanis named on the following pages. It is a Church of the East DIOCESAN calendar, the same kind of witness as the ACOE Diocese of California calendars that carried the 59 COE confirmations on 2026-09-03. No confirmation ever rested on it under the wrong label, but a future session looking for an Anglican witness would have found it and cited it.

HAPGOOD.label: Hapgood, Service Book of the Holy Orthodox-Catholic Apostolic (Greco-Russian) Church, 1906
HAPGOOD.path: NOT IN REPO -- archive.org item ServiceBookOfHolyOrthodoxChurchByHapgood; Appendix B pp.592-615 supplied by Josh as an upload 2026-09-04
HAPGOOD.notes: Public domain (Emory/Pitts digitisation states the online edition is not protected by copyright). Slavic recension, matching Charter section 9's implemented baseline. Approved by Josh 2026-09-04 as the governing source for Byzantine explanatory content in data/explanations/byzantine.json. Appendix B is the book's own numbered explanation apparatus. LIMITS, from Hapgood's own Preface: she omitted even the skeleton of the Midnight Service and Little Vespers, and left Vespers largely in skeleton form -- so Appendix B does not explain the Midnight Office or either Compline. Not a hymnographic source; Lambertsen remains the governing source for this lane's hymnography.
